**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make reaction activation atomic**

When two retries with `emrrActive=true` arrive concurrently for the same party, moment, and reaction type, both transactions can finish this unlocked lookup before either inserts, so both conclude that the row is absent. The unique `EventMomentReaction` constraint then makes one insert fail with a database conflict and surface as a 500 instead of providing the promised idempotent success; use an atomic upsert or lock the party/moment reaction state before checking and inserting.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Redact other users' reaction identity**

For any moment containing reactions from multiple parties, this unconditional `Just` serializes every `reactorPartyId` through both `loadEventMoments` and `loadMomentDTO`, whose mapper has no viewer context. This contradicts the API contract in `tdf-hq/docs/openapi/api.yaml`, which promises anonymous counts and identity only for the caller's own reaction, and exposes other fans' party identifiers; pass the authenticated party into the projection and null `emrPartyId` and `emrCreatedAt` for non-owned rows.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Scope the Slack webhook to the notification step**

When `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` is configured, declaring it at job scope injects the webhook credential into every step, including checkout, setup-node, and the mutable `superfly/flyctl-actions/setup-flyctl@master` action. Any compromised or accidentally verbose setup action can read or exfiltrate the webhook even though only the Slack notification needs it; gate the notification with a non-secret flag or output and keep the actual secret in that action's step-level environment.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Replay queued onboarding completion on public routes**

When `completeOnboardingProgress` fails after a durable action succeeds on `/fans`, `/a/*`, or `/inicio`, this catch leaves the new local-storage entry queued, but `retryPendingFirstValueCompletion` is invoked only by `routes/AppShell.tsx`; those pages are registered in `routes/publicRoutes.tsx` and never mount `Shell`. Merely coming back online therefore does not retry, so onboarding stays incomplete and first-value analytics are omitted until a reload or an unrelated protected-page visit; install the recovery hook in a provider shared by public routes as well.

body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Backfill evidence for already-active reactions**

When an onboarding-eligible user already has this reaction—for example, it was created during the onboarding window by the pre-deployment handler—an idempotent `emrrActive=true` request takes this branch but the `isNothing existingSameReaction` guard skips both inserts. `onboardingFirstValueEvidenceAt` recognizes only a corresponding `EngagementEvent`, so these users remain unable to complete the `moment_reaction` first-value step despite having performed the action. Backfill legacy rows using their stored creation time or insert the missing evidence when an active row has none.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep provider outages distinct from empty search results**

When MusicBrainz or Discogs exhausts retries, returning `value: null` here makes both `researchInventoryIdentity` and `researchArtist` pass that null into `publicProviderSearchSources`, which interprets it as a successful search with no exact match. In production this persists `musicbrainz_search_no_exact_match` or `discogs_search_no_exact_match` evidence whose attribution falsely claims the provider returned no candidate, even though it was unavailable; preserve an unavailable state or suppress those no-match sources for providers listed in `providerOutages`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retain failed dismissal state across account switches**

When Party A dismisses onboarding, switches to Party B before the completion request fails, and later returns to A without unmounting this page, this early return leaves `dismissedOnboardingPartyId` set to A. The server still considers A incomplete, but the banner and retry warning remain hidden for the rest of the component lifetime; preserve the failed state per party or clear A's optimistic dismissal even while another party is active.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

FOR UPDATE, covering the absent-reaction case; SQLite takes its writer lock via the parent-row update. The mutation and engagement evidence remain in one transaction. Final-SHA CI passed all 2,542 backend examples, including activation/replay/evidence coverage: https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/34916758923. body: Fixed by repairing missing engagement evidence for an already-active reaction using the stored reaction creation timestamp. Matching evidence is checked transactionally, so repeated activation does not duplicate evidence or manufacture a new action time. The regression `repairs legacy reaction evidence once without changing the original action time` passed on b246a8fb8; final CI passed all 2,542 backend examples: https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/34916758923.

Fixed in 5bceb329f by storing dismissal/failure state per party. A late failure remains available when that party returns, while another party's dismissal or error is preserved independently; the active-party guard for successful query-cache updates remains intact. Regressions cover A → B → A after failure and two accounts failing out of order. Both reproduced the original defect and passed after the change; fresh CI then passed the complete onboarding file and all 206 UI suites / 1,968 tests: https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/34922297080. Local resource-related timeout limitations remain documented separately in the PR report.
